The new ingredients are a pointwise linearization of the collapsing action at regular orbits, an invariant harmonic transverse coordinate compatible with finite isotropy, and an exactly equivariant orbit coordinate built from an elementary rounding-and-doubling argument in the collapsing deck group.

entries.name: S-squareful values of binary quadratic forms
entries.abstract: Shute showed that the leading constant in the asymptotic formula for squareful values of the form $ax^2+by^2$ does not match with the conjecture established by Pieropan, Smeets, Tanimoto and Várilly-Alvarado. In this paper, $S$-squareful values of this form are considered for $S$ the set of primes that divide $a$ and $b$. We prove an asymptotic formula for these numbers and show that the leading constant of the asymptotic formula still does not match the conjecture. Furthermore, we consider the updated conjecture established by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash, and Tanimoto regarding the leading constant for Campana points in the given setting and show that this constant is consistent with our computed constant.

entries.name: On the Hodge conjecture for hyper-Kähler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by four
entries.abstract: We prove the Hodge conjecture for all hyper-Kähler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by 4 and all of their powers. To this end, we show that such hyper-Kähler varieties are homologically motivated by their intermediate Jacobians.

entries.name: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
entries.abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.

entries.name: Minimal Control Time of Large Generic Quantum Systems at Critical Spectral Growth
entries.abstract: The minimal time needed to steer a closed quantum system between two arbitrary states is a fundamental performance limit of quantum control. For single-input bilinear Schrödinger systems of dimension $d$ with unbounded controls, this state-to-state control time is bounded from above by the weight $M_d$ of a minimum spanning tree (MST) built from the drift Hamiltonian written in the eigenbasis of the control Hamiltonian. We ask whether the control time of a \emph{generic} system, whose control Hamiltonian has a Haar-distributed eigenbasis, vanishes as $d\to\infty$ in the critical regime of drift eigenvalues growing as $k^{3/2}$. We prove that the finite clusters of the interaction matrix are asymptotically independent Gaussians, analyse the resulting independent surrogate model, for which $M_d \asymp (\ln d)^{-1/2}$ with an explicit finite-size expansion predicting $M_d\sqrt{\ln d}\to 10/3$, and test the exact Haar model by Monte Carlo simulations up to $d=18101$. The exact and surrogate models are statistically indistinguishable in mean at all tested dimensions, and both are consistent with the predicted limit, supporting the conjecture that the control time vanishes, albeit only logarithmically.

entries.name: Congruence properties modulo powers of 3 for designated summands in partitions into odd parts
entries.abstract: Let $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$ denote the total number of tagged parts over all partitions of $n$ into odd parts with designated summands. Using $3$-dissection identities and coefficient extraction, we obtain explicit polynomial expansions for the generating functions of two infinite families of arithmetic subsequences of $\textup{PDO}_\textup{t}(n)$. We establish lower bounds for the $3$-adic valuations of the polynomial coefficients, thereby proving two infinite families of congruences conjectured by Lin (J. Number Theory,~2018). We then estimate the $3$-adic valuations of two-by-two determinants formed from consecutive coefficient vectors. These estimates yield two infinite families of internal congruences modulo high powers of $3$. The internal congruences and the initial generating functions also establish the generating-function congruences conjectured by Singh and Barman (Ramanujan J.,~2025).

entries.name: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
entries.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. In 2004, Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$ and determine all subsets of maximum size in $C_n^2$ that contain no $n$ elements with sum zero.

entries.name: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
entries.abstract: The defect of a complex Hadamard matrix is the real dimension of the solution space obtained by linearizing the row orthogonality equations in the phases of the entries, with the first row and column fixed. It is known that defect zero implies isolation up to Hadamard equivalence. The converse, whether every isolated complex Hadamard matrix has defect zero, was open and is the square-matrix case of a conjecture of Banica, Ozteke and Pittau. We answer this question in the negative. We exhibit a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of order 13 with entries among the sixth roots of unity and show that it is isolated and has defect one. We prove isolation by showing that no nonzero solution of the linearized equations satisfies the second order condition obtained by the second author for directions of convergence of sequences of Hadamard matrices. In the language of commuting squares of matrix algebras, the example shows that an isolated commuting square can fail the span condition introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation.

entries.name: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture holds for all complex reflection groups
entries.abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups, and we treat the remaining case of the infinite series, so that the conjecture now holds for all complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra; they provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups, and a model for computing in the Hecke algebras. The canonical trace is then obtained from other bases: generalisations of the $z$-bases of earlier work for the smaller groups, and bases built along towers of parabolic subgroups for the largest ones. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

entries.name: Exact Hausdorff and Packing Dimensions of $k$-Singular Matrices
entries.abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of $k$-singular $m\times n$ matrices for all $m,n\geq1$ and $2\leq k\leq m+n-1$. Such matrices are characterized by the $(k-1)$st successive minimum tending to zero and the $(k+1)$st tending to infinity along an associated diagonal-flow orbit. The exact formula was announced by Das--Fishman--Simmons--Urbański in 2017 and formulated as a conjecture in their 2024 paper, which proves the matching Hausdorff-dimension lower bound. We prove the matching packing-dimension upper bound, resolving their Conjecture~5.1. The proof uses their variational principle together with a linear potential that corrects the local contraction rate. The corrected rate is nondecreasing under mergers of adjacent equality blocks that preserve a separating gap, reducing the estimate to two-block configurations. Secant-line estimates at integer points then allow us to choose a single pair of potential coefficients that controls both possible separating gaps. The dimension formula remains valid after excluding trivially singular matrices.

entries.name: The Boundary Conjecture for Smoothable Alexandrov Spaces
entries.abstract: We prove that in a noncollapsed limit of complete Riemannian manifolds with $\sec\geκ$, each boundary component of a compact full-dimensional convex body, equipped with its intrinsic length metric, has Alexandrov curvature at least $κ$. We also consider such a body in the limit of a noncollapsed sequence of Alexandrov spaces with curvature at least $κ$. If $κ>0$ or the boundary of the body is strongly convex, we show that the body can be approximated by convex bodies in the given sequence.

entries.name: The spectrum of codegree Turán densities of 3-graphs
entries.abstract: The \emph{minimum codegree} $δ_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Turán density} $γ(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $δ_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $α\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Turán density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_α$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $γ(\mathcal{F}')>α$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_α$. This resolves the $3$-graph case of a conjecture of Mubayi and Zhao, the only case that remained open after recent work of Lin and Zhou. (Li and Liu earlier determined the codegree Turán spectrum in every uniformity $k\ge 4$ and, very recently, they determined the spectrum for $k=3$ independently of us.) We also consider \emph{positive codegree Turán density}, defined analogously by taking the minimum only over $(k-1)$-sets contained in at least one edge. We prove that there is an absolute constant $c<1$ such that, for every integer $k\geq3$, every real number in $[c,1)$ is the positive codegree Turán density of a $k$-graph family. This is done by presenting a construction with a relatively short proof, without optimising the value of $c$.

entries.name: The $T1$ theorem under Dini regularity
entries.abstract: We prove the $T1$ theorem for Calderón-Zygmund operators under the classical Dini regularity condition on the kernel, solving a longstanding open problem in singular integral theory.

entries.name: The optimal exponent in the Erdős--Fuchs theorem for $k$-fold sums
entries.abstract: Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer. For an infinite set $A$ of nonnegative integers and a real number $x\ge0$, let $r_k(A,x)$ be the number of $k$-tuples $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\in A^k$ satisfying $a_1+\cdots +a_k\le x$. In this paper, we prove that $r_k(A,x)=cx+o(x^{(1-1/k)^2})$ is impossible for any real number $c>0$. The exponent $(1-1/k)^2$ is best possible for $k\ge3$ by a recent result of Guo and Yan. Moreover, we obtain a mean-square estimate of $r_k(A,x)-cx$ and confirm a conjecture of Chen and Tang for every $k\ge3$.

entries.name: Unified Schur multiple zeta functions
entries.abstract: We define symmetric multiple zeta values, unified zeta functions, and finite zeta values in the Schur setting. We establish a Jacobi--Trudi formula and a Giambelli formula for unified Schur multiple zeta functions, and we show that there is a one-to-one correspondence between finite and symmetric Schur multiple zeta values under the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture. We also show a vanishing property for a symmetric sum of finite Schur multiple zeta values, generalizing a result obtained by Hoffman for finite multiple zeta values.

entries.name: Minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous and bounded
entries.abstract: We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.

entries.name: Sharpness of the Brjuno Condition for Hyperbolic Bishop Surfaces
entries.abstract: Let $μ\in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $|μ|=1$, and assume that $μ$ is not a root of unity and is not Brjuno. Let $Q_γ$ denote the Bishop quadric with $γ= 1/\sqrt{2+μ+μ^{-1}} > 1/2$. Gong and Stolovitch conjectured that there exists a real-analytic surface in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with Moser--Webster invariant $μ$ that is formally but not holomorphically equivalent to $Q_γ$. We prove this conjecture.

entries.name: Gaudin's determinantal norm formula and Hall--Littlewood polynomials
entries.abstract: The Hall--Littlewood polynomials are orthogonal with respect to a discrete measure stemming from a discretization of the Lieb--Liniger model that describes $q$-bosons on the circle. This note establishes a previously conjectured Gaudin-type determinantal formula for their quadratic norms.

entries.name: The monodromy conjecture for remarkable poles
entries.abstract: We prove the strong monodromy conjecture for the remarkable numbers of a regular function f on a smooth complex variety. We show more generally that the log canonical modification of f computes the remarkable numbers and gives roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of f.

entries.name: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
entries.abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g λ_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8π^2/\sqrt{3} + 8π$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

entries.name: Total curvature and area growth of entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space
entries.abstract: We prove that entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ have infinite total curvature. Since their Gauss curvature is negative, this means that their intrinsic area growth is not quadratic, as conjectured by Pérez, Rodríguez and the author. It follows that vertical planes are the only orientable complete stable surfaces with constant mean curvature and quadratic area growth in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$, and this classification is extended to surfaces with critical and supercritical constant mean curvature in the homogeneous spaces $\mathbb{E}(κ,τ)$. We also prove that the height of an entire minimal graph in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ grows at most quadratically, as conjectured by Nelli and the author, whence the extrinsic and cylindrical area growths of such a graph are exactly cubic. Our arguments rely on the conformal Calabi-Lee duality between minimal graphs in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ and spacelike graphs with constant mean curvature $τ$ in the Lorentz-Minkowski space $\mathbb{L}^3$, for which we also get sharp gradient estimates.

entries.name: Kushel--Tyaglov's problem, sharp Schoenberg-type inequalities and majorization relations between zeros and critical points
entries.abstract: In this paper, we give a purely complex-analytic proof of Schoenberg's conjecture. We also determine the sharp constants in Schoenberg-type inequalities for every real exponent $p>0$ and every degree $n\ge2$, and characterize all corresponding extremal configurations. In particular, we confirm two conjectures posed in \cite{TZ25} and provide a complete solution to a problem of Kushel and Tyaglov. Furthermore, we introduce the tool of weighted weak majorization and establish, under the zero-centroid condition, new weak-majorization relations between the moduli of the critical points and those of the zeros. As consequences of these relations, we obtain refinements of several known results.

entries.name: $k$-ary Legendre pairs
entries.abstract: We study $k$-ary Legendre pairs and derive arithmetic restrictions on their existence and balance. For an odd prime $p$, we determine the component sums of a $p$-ary Legendre pair and show that, after normalization, each component has fixed symbol composition. As a consequence, every $p$-ary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ yields a Butson Hadamard matrix $H(2p,2\ell+2)$. For ternary Legendre pairs we combine fixed-content necklaces, integral-PAF symmetries, exact half-frequency restrictions, compression-decompression, and PSD tests. These reductions lead to ternary Legendre pairs for every admissible length $\ell\le32$. We conjecture that ternary Legendre pairs exist for every admissible length.

entries.name: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
entries.abstract: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.

entries.name: $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic intersections of $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds with perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces
entries.abstract: We show that transverse intersections between smooth $\mathbb{C}_p$-analytic manifolds in $\mathbb{C}_p^n$ and perfectoid Banach--Colmez spaces of complementary $\mathbb{C}_p$-dimension are $n$-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}_p$-analytic manifolds. In the case of the Banach--Colmez space $\mathrm{BC}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$, this is a strong form of the relativistic $p$-adic sunscreen conjecture. These results hold more generally with $\mathbb{C}_p$ replaced by an arbitrary complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and we also establish some non-linear analogs for infinite level Lubin--Tate spaces.

entries.name: Uniqueness and comparison for a singular parabolic equation with a concave nonlinearity
entries.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for $\partial_t u-Δu=|x|^{-γ}u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, with $0<q<1$, $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$ and nonnegative initial data $u_0\in C_0(\mathbb{R}^N)$. Since $s\mapsto s^q$ is not Lipschitz continuous at the origin, the uniqueness of nonnegative solutions is a delicate issue. {For $u_0\not\equiv0$, it was known for small values of $γ$ and, more recently, under the additional condition $γ<N(1-q)$.} We prove that, for $u_0\not\equiv0$, uniqueness holds on the whole range $0<γ<\min\{2,N\}$, which settles a conjecture of the authors. In fact, we establish a comparison principle between bounded subsolutions and supersolutions which are bounded from below by a multiple of the profile $t^{1/(1-q)}(|x|+\sqrt t\,)^{-γ/(1-q)}$. We then describe completely the set of nonnegative solutions emanating from $u_0\equiv0$: it consists of the trivial solution, of a unique positive solution $U$, and of the delayed copies $U(\cdot,(t-τ)_+)$, $τ>0$. The solution $U$ is radially symmetric and self-similar, it obeys {two-sided pointwise bounds by multiples of the same profile}, and it is the limit of the solutions with nontrivial data as the data decrease to zero. Finally, we show that $U$ describes the large-time behavior of every nontrivial solution. The proofs replace the singular Gronwall inequality used in earlier work by a quotient estimate which exploits the concavity of $s\mapsto s^q$ and requires no smallness condition.

entries.name: $K3$ Picard--Fuchs equations with initial conditions in the Hodge line
entries.abstract: Lam and Litt conjectured that a formal horizontal section of a Gauss--Manin connection is algebraic if and only if it is integral, if and only if it is $ω(p)$-integral. We prove it for families of $K3$ surfaces over a finitely generated $\mathbb Z$-algebra in a number field, when the initial condition lies in the Hodge line. In this case, all three conditions are equivalent to the vanishing of the Higgs field on the Hodge line. Along the way, we show that a smooth projective family $X\to S$ with $H^0(X_s,T_{X_s})=0$ is constant on an étale neighborhood of $s$ if and only if its Kodaira--Spencer class vanishes near $s$.

entries.name: $C^*(\mathbb{F}_2\times\mathbb{F}_2)$ fails the local lifting property
entries.abstract: We prove that the full group \(C^*\)-algebra \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) fails the local lifting property for all integers \(k,m\ge2\), and therefore disprove Ozawa's Strong Kirchberg Conjecture. Our proof is inspired by a construction of Ioana concerning Hilbert--Schmidt stability. We then strengthen this result by showing that \(C^*(\F_k\times\F_m)\) does not locally embed into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\). Consequently, the lifting property, the local lifting property, and local embeddability into \(C^*(\F_\infty)\) are not preserved under maximal tensor products.

entries.name: A proof of the chemical recurrence conjecture in two dimensions
entries.abstract: At the microscopic level, the dynamics of a network of chemical reactions can be modeled, in the well-mixed case, as a continuous-time Markov chain. This process counts the number of particles in each of the $d$ species as a function of time, and its state-dependent, polynomial jump rates are determined by the structure of the underlying reaction graph. Networks of chemical reactions whose reaction graphs are the union of strongly connected components are called \emph{weakly reversible}. The long-standing \emph{chemical recurrence conjecture} states that if a network is weakly reversible, then the associated Markov chain is positive recurrent. We prove this conjecture for $d=2$.

entries.name: Quadratic periods after adjoining one move to a fixed subtraction game
entries.abstract: Zhang conjectured that adjoining one move $c$ to a fixed subtraction set $S$ gives a Grundy sequence whose least preperiod and period are both $O_S(c)$. For every $q=20+9s$ with $s\ge0$, take $S=\{3,6,q-3\}$. Along $c=qk+1$ with $k\ge2$, the Grundy and win/loss sequences are periodic from heap zero with common least period $(k+2)(c+6)-11$, asymptotic to $c^2/q$. For $\{3,6,17\}$ we determine both least periods and preperiods for every positive $c$ and verify the complete table in Lean. Fixed bases with the same entire Grundy sequence realize infinitely many distinct positive quadratic coefficients for the augmented period. A second fixed triple gives a quadratic Grundy preperiod while the win/loss sequence repeats from heap zero. A third has a quadratic Grundy period but only a linear win/loss period. For an arbitrary fixed $S$, a linear bound on both Grundy invariants implies eventual affine formulas with integer coefficients on residue classes. The same finite-state method extends four numerical tables of Zhang. We also give the entire augmented sequence for $c>\max S$ when the losing heaps of $S$ are exactly the multiples of a fixed integer.

entries.name: Idempotent generically stable measures in NSOP$_1$ groups
entries.abstract: We prove the Idempotent Measure Conjecture for type-definable groups in theories whose Keisler randomization is NSOP$_1$. More precisely, every global idempotent frequency interpretation measure on such a group is the unique left-invariant and the unique right-invariant measure concentrating on its type-definable stabilizer. In particular, its support is a left-simple convolution semigroup and has a unique minimal left ideal. The announced theorem of Ben Yaacov, Chernikov and Ramsey that randomization preserves NSOP$_1$ (proof in the appendix) yields the corresponding conclusion for all type-definable groups in NSOP$_1$ theories.

entries.name: Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
entries.abstract: We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).

entries.name: Counting elliptic curves by discriminant
entries.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula with a power saving for the number of $\mathbb{Q}$-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}$ ordered by minimal discriminant, assuming the $abc$ conjecture. Unconditionally, we obtain the same asymptotic for the curves with $|Δ_{\min}(E)| \le X$ and $c_4(E) \le X^{8/3 - δ}$ for any fixed $δ> 0$, by obtaining new bounds for the number of integral points $(c_4, c_6)$ near the cusp $c_4^3 = c_6^2$.

entries.name: Fake surfaces for some potential Andrews-Curtis counterexamples
entries.abstract: Andrews and Curtis famously conjectured that every contractible $2$-complex $3$-deforms to a point and, in fact, it suffices to consider contractible closed fake surfaces. The traditional potential counterexamples are given as balanced presentations of the trivial group. In this article, we construct closed fake surfaces for the Akbulut-Kirby family of potential counterexamples using geodesic loops in a metric classifying space for the $3$-strand braid group. Concretely we construct a $(2n+1)$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_n$ with a cyclically symmetric $1$-skeleton. Our $7$-vertex fake surface for $\mathrm{AK}_3$ is the simplest fake surface whose Andrews-Curtis status is unknown.

entries.name: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
entries.abstract: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.

entries.name: Symbolic Proof Compression and Fractal Universality: A Conditional Non-Constructive Refutation of the Riemann Hypothesis
entries.abstract: Building on S.~C.~Woon's (1994) fractal and symbolic reformulation of Voronin's Universality Theorem, we construct a formal, non-constructive proof-by-contradiction architecture exploring the Riemann Hypothesis ($\mathsf{RH}$). Woon's Corollary~3 permits arbitrary finite binary strings to be encoded into nowhere-vanishing exponential waveforms on a closed disk inside the critical strip. Combining effective upper bounds for Voronin universality (Good, Garunkštis) with Cauchy-integral Taylor decoding yields an explicit finite rational grid $\mathcal{G}_{L_0}$ below an effective ceiling $H_{\mathrm{crit}}(L_0)$ within which every formal proof of bit-length at most $L_0$ is imprinted with zero flipped digits. We introduce a conjectural \emph{Zeta-Universal Symbolic Proof Compression Hypothesis} ($\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$), positing that the global regularity implied by $\mathsf{RH}$ compresses true $Π_1^0$ statements about $ζ(s)$ into $\mathsf{ZFC}$ derivations of bounded length $L_0$. Assuming classical logic and $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$, Gödel--Carnap diagonalization over bounded zeta-encoded provability yields a contradiction. The self-referential result converts a digital encoding framework with any uniform proof-compression principle for RH into an immediate non-constructive refutation of RH. Given that, with human input and computer assistance, $\mathsf{RH}$ has been formally verified in the Lean theorem prover strictly within constructive logic, this contradiction does not refute $\mathsf{RH}$. Instead, it falsifies $\mathsf{SPC}_{\mathsf{RH}}$. We conclude by isolating the exact proof-theoretic obstruction---Pudlák's lower bound on bounded reflection proofs---showing why the analytic regularity of $\mathsf{RH}$ cannot compress logical self-reference, and exposing the limits of applying the Law of Excluded Middle to uncomputably bounded searches.

entries.name: Matrix Criteria for Mordell--Weil Ranks of Quartic Twists of $y^2=x^3+x$ with Root Number $-1$
entries.abstract: We study the Mordell--Weil ranks of quartic twists $E_a:y^2=x^3+ax$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with global root number $-1$. For $D$ a product of $n\ge2$ distinct odd primes, a $2$-isogeny descent yields unconditional rank bounds for $E_D$, $E_{-D}$, and $E_{-2D}$ in terms of matrices over $\mathbb{F}_2$ defined by additive Legendre symbols. Under suitable congruence and matrix-rank conditions, these curves have rank at most one, and rank one assuming the Mordell--Weil parity conjecture. For $E_{-2D}$, an additional explicit square condition establishes rank one unconditionally. Our results extend earlier two-prime criteria to arbitrary numbers of prime factors and further to fourth-power-free coefficients $H=\prod_{i=1}^n\ell_i^{e_i}$, where $e_i\in\{1,3\}$.

entries.name: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
entries.abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, χ_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, André, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

entries.name: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
entries.abstract: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.

entries.name: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
entries.abstract: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.

entries.name: An $O(n^{-1/2})$ remainder for the Chow--Robbins stopping boundary
entries.abstract: We sharpen the asymptotic approximation to the optimal stopping boundary in the Chow--Robbins game, proving the inverse-square-root remainder conjectured by Elton. The proof combines an exactly harmonic integral for simple random walk with a Catalan first-passage renewal identity. Averaging the stopping defect over one spatial period removes its leading lattice dependence, and a coupling of states at equal depth transfers this cancellation to the renewal sum. Consequently, the explicit integer stopping rule can fail at no more than a constant times the square root of the number of observation times.

entries.name: Tensor powers of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, zonotopal algebras, and quiver varieties
entries.abstract: In this paper we study the $m$-th tensor power ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(q)$. To do that we use the connection between tensor products of unipotent characters and the cohomology of certain quiver varieties for star-shaped quivers \cite{L2}\cite{LRV}. We prove that the cohomology ring of the quiver variety associated to ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ is generated by its tautological classes. We use this to prove that this cohomology ring is isomorphic to a central zonotopal algebra. We then deduce a combinatorial formula for the multiplicities of unipotent characters in ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$. This formula has been conjectured by the second author when $m=2$.

entries.name: A Proof of the Ovals Conjecture
entries.abstract: We prove that the lowest eigenvalue of the periodic Schrödinger operator $-\partial_s^2+κ^2$ on a closed curve of length $\ell$ is at least $4π^2/\ell^2$. Equality holds precisely for the family of ovals described by Benguria and Loss. The proof uses a new comparison argument for scalar ordinary differential equations.

entries.name: Spectral characterizations of sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds
entries.abstract: Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau, in Conjecture 3.9 of [Springer Proc. Math. Stat. 88 (2014): 147--207], asked whether a Faber--Krahn inequality and matching bounds for the bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on balls characterize sub-Gaussian heat kernel upper bounds. We give a counterexample on the Euclidean plane. Our counterexample uses a planar diffusion associated with a Dirichlet form from the work of Li and Sun in [Ann. Appl. Probab. 34 (2024), 4193--4236]. The bottom of the Dirichlet spectrum on every ball of radius $r$ is comparable to $r^{-2}$ meanwhile for balls centered on the $x_1$-axis, the mean exit time starting at the center is comparable to $r^3$ as $r\downarrow0$. This also shows that the exit-time hypotheses used to characterize heat kernel upper bounds in [Stochastic Process. Appl. 189 (2025): 104707] and [Math. Nachr. 299 (2026): 2566--2589] cannot be omitted. We then give a novel spectral characterization of heat kernel upper bounds in terms of the first Dirichlet eigenpair of balls. In particular, on an unbounded proper geodesic Dirichlet space with volume doubling, reverse volume doubling and a scale-$r^β$ Poincaré inequality, the heat kernel upper estimate is equivalent to $λ(B(x,r))\asymp r^{-β}$ and a uniform comparison between the supremum of a nonnegative first eigenfunction and its value at $x$. Under elliptic Harnack inequality, we also prove that the mean exit-time scale on balls is equivalent to the scale on the bottom of the spectrum on balls. This proves Conjecture~4.15 of Grigor'yan, Hu and Lau. The Euclidean planar example given above also disproves the eigenvalue version of their Conjecture~4.16 on a characterization of the parabolic harnack inequality. We end by showing that our spectral conditions gives the correct characterization.

entries.name: Stokes corners and the global structure of steady rotating waves in annular domains
entries.abstract: We study steady rotating water waves in a planar annulus, in the model of radial gravity and constant vorticity introduced by Li and the author. The stream function is harmonic, and the free surface carries the Bernoulli condition $p_0^2|\nablaΨ|^2=Q_α(S)$ with $Q_α(R)=(R-r_-)(R-r_+)$. We first settle the crest shape. For $α\neqα_\pm$, every stagnation point lies on the circle $R=r_-$, and the surface forms a symmetric $120^\circ$ corner there. At $α=α_\pm$ the corner is a right angle. The same holds for limits of smooth solutions and, in the lower region, for overhanging waves. We then study the global bifurcation continuum. Its waves are monotone from crest to trough, and they always cross the laminar circle. Hence there is no secondary bifurcation, and the parameter stays above an explicit floor. The continuum ends in an extreme wave, overturns, or degenerates; the last case is excluded for $c_0>γ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$. An annular Nekrasov equation and an invariant Keady--Norbury cone give a slope bound below $90^\circ$ whenever the Nekrasov weight is nonnegative on the waves. A sharpened angular flow-force estimate keeps the troughs where this weight is nonnegative, for every $γ\in(0,1)$ above the floor. Hence, whenever $c_0>γ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$, the existence half of the Stokes conjecture holds: the continuum contains an extreme wave with a $120^\circ$ Stokes crest. In the remaining band $\sinh^2γ<c_0\leγ^2e^{2γ}/(1+γ)^2$ the result is conditional: the continuum ends in such a wave unless its parameter degenerates to the value at which the effective gravity vanishes on the stagnation circle, and we cannot exclude this degeneration. We also show that the bifurcation is supercritical for every $γ\in(0,1)$.

papers.name: On Prime Values of Bunyakovsky's Polynomials and Prime Products of Schinzel's Polynomials
papers.abstract: First, we prove a theorem of the number of primes in short intervals with a much more accurate estimation of prime numbers, the error range of which is less than $x^{1/2-0.0327283}$ for $x\geq10^{41}$. The theorem states as follows: Given a positive real number $β$ that determines a real number $x_β$ by $e(\log x_β)^{3}/x_β^{0.0327283}=β$, let $Φ(x):=βx^{1/2}$ for $x\geq x_β$ where $Φ(x):=x^{1/2}$ when let $β=1$. Then there are \[ \frac{π(x+Φ(x))-π(x)}{Φ(x)/\log x}=1+O(\frac{1}{\log x}) \] and \[ \lim_{x \to \infty}\frac{π(x+Φ(x))-π(x)}{Φ(x)/\log x}=1. \] Next, based on the theorem, Bunyakovsky's polynomials, Schinzel's polynomials, and Schinzel's polynomials with a negative leading coefficient are researched. Results show that (1) given a Bunyakovsky's polynomial $f(x)$, $f(m)$ is prime for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (2) given a Schinzel's polynomial $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{k}f_{i}(x)$, all numbers $f_{1}(m)$, $f_{2}(m)$, $\ldots$, $f_{k}(m)$ are primes for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (3) given a Schinzel's polynomial $f(x)=\prod_{i=1}^{k}f_{i}(x)$ with a negative leading coefficient for $f_{k}(x)$ and positive leading coefficients for others, all numbers $f_{1}(m)$, $f_{2}(m)$, $\ldots$, $f_{k}(m)$ are primes for infinitely many positive integers $m$, (4) so some other conjectures in the number theory are proved.

papers.name: Koszul duality in exact categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish Koszul duality-type results in the setting of chain complexes in exact categories. In particular, we prove generalisations of Vallette's Koszul duality theorem and Koszul duality along the lines of Lurie and Pridham. We also prove a connective version. We conclude with some applications. These include our main example, the category of complete bornological spaces over a Banach field, as well as a sketch of deformation theory in formal geometry.

papers.name: Geometric Manin's Conjecture for Fano 3-Folds
papers.abstract: We classify families of free rational curves on all smooth Fano threefolds over the complex numbers. In particular, we prove the family of very free rational curves representing any fixed numerical curve class is either irreducible or empty. This proves Geometric Manin's Conjecture in dimension three. For general Fano threefolds of each deformation type, our results allow us to explicitly count the number of components of the moduli space of irreducible, geometrically rational curves, which may not be free, representing any numerical class.

papers.name: Oriented trees in $O(k \sqrt{k})$-chromatic digraphs, a subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1980, Burr conjectured that every directed graph with chromatic number $2k-2$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$ as a subdigraph. Burr showed that chromatic number $(k-1)^2$ suffices, and this was later improved to $\frac{k^2}{2} - \frac{k}{2} + 1$ by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares-Sales, Reed and Thomassé. We prove the first subquadratic bound for Burr's conjecture: every digraph with chromatic number $\frac{8}{3} k \sqrt{k} + 7k$ contains any oriented tree of order $k$. Moreover, we provide improved bounds of $\sqrt{4/3} k \sqrt{k}+k/2$ for arborescences, and $\frac{(b+3)}{2}k$ for paths with $b$ blocks.

papers.name: The standard generators of the tetrahedron algebra and their look-alikes
papers.abstract: The tetrahedron algebra $\boxtimes$ is an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra defined by generators $\{x_{ij} \mid i, j \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}, i \neq j\}$ and some relations, including the Dolan-Grady relations. These twelve generators are called standard. We introduce a type of element in $\boxtimes$ that ``looks like'' a standard generator. For mutually distinct $h, i, j, k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, consider the standard generator $x_{ij}$ of $\boxtimes$. An element $ξ\in \boxtimes$ is called $x_{ij}$-like whenever both (i) $ξ$ commutes with $x_{ij}$; (ii) $ξ$ and $x_{hk}$ satisfy a Dolan-Grady relation. Pick mutually distinct $i,j,k \in \{0,1,2,3\}$. In our main result, we find an attractive basis for $\boxtimes$ with the property that every basis element is either $x_{ij}$-like or $x_{jk}$-like or $x_{ki}$-like. We discuss this basis from multiple points of view.

papers.name: Enumerating 1324-avoiders with few inversions
papers.abstract: We enumerate the numbers $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324)$ of 1324-avoiding $n$-permutations with exactly $k$ inversions for all $k$ and $n \geq (k+7)/2$. The result depends on a structural characterization of such permutations in terms of a new notion of almost-decomposability. In particular, our enumeration verifies half of a conjecture of Claesson, Jelínek and Steingrímsson, according to which $\mathrm{av}_n^k(1324) \leq \mathrm{av}_{n+1}^k(1324)$ for all $n$ and $k$. Proving also the other half would improve the best known upper bound for the exponential growth rate of the number of $1324$-avoiders from $13.5$ to approximately $13.002$.

papers.name: Rational Curves on Coindex 3 Fano Varieties
papers.abstract: We describe the moduli space of rational curves on smooth Fano varieties of coindex 3. For varieties of dimension 5 or greater, we prove the moduli space has a single irreducible component for each effective numerical class of curves. For varieties of dimension 4, we describe families of rational curves in terms of Fujita's $a$-invariant. Our results verify Lehmann and Tanimoto's Geometric Manin's Conjecture for all smooth coindex 3 Fano varieties over the complex numbers.

papers.name: Structural Origins of Cubic Complexity in Pebble Motion
papers.abstract: The pebble motion problem (PMP) asks whether labeled pebbles on a graph can be rearranged by moving them to adjacent empty vertices (blanks). Kornhauser, Miller, and Spirakis (FOCS 1984) proved the tight $Θ(N^3)$ worst-case bound on $N$-vertex graphs and asked for efficient approximation of move counts. Whether this bound is tight on trees remained open for over four decades. We give the first $\mathrm{o}(N^3)$ upper bound on trees: every feasible instance admits an $\mathrm{O}(N^2\log N)$-move solution, constructible in time linear in its length, within a logarithmic factor of the known $Ω(N^2)$ lower bound. We extend the tree method to a hybrid algorithm with structure-dependent bounds for general graphs. When $2\leq N-n=\mathrm{O}(1)$, every instance on a feasible puzzle admits an $\mathrm{O}(n\,\mathrm{CL}(G)\,\mathrm{D}(G))$-move solution, where $n$ counts pebbles, $\mathrm{D}(G)$ is the diameter, and $\mathrm{CL}(G)$ is the maximum shortest-cycle length through a vertex. For square grids, this matches the classical $\mathrm{O}(N^{3/2})$ bound. Cubic complexity requires $\mathrm{O}(1)$ blanks. We develop cut-vertex reconfiguration and a closure theorem under arbitrary ear extensions. These imply that cubic complexity requires a unique biconnected component $X$ of order $Θ(N)$ with reconfiguration cost $Θ(N^3)$; the total attachment through each cut vertex of $G$ in $X$ has bounded order. Moreover, $X$ has no cycle of unbounded sublinear order, and intersecting $Θ(N)$-cycles in $X$ share at least $N-n$ vertices. Attaching bounded-size connected graphs along $\mathrm{O}(1)$ individual edges of a $Θ(N)$-cycle yields cubic complexity for feasible puzzles, whereas two $Θ(N)$-cycles sharing one vertex have worst-case complexity $Θ(N^2\log N)$. We conjecture that this construction characterizes the cubic regime.

papers.name: Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs: resilience and approximate decompositions
papers.abstract: Dirac's classical theorem asserts that, for $n\ge 3$, any $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $\frac{n}{2}$ is Hamiltonian. Furthermore, if we additionally assume that such graphs are regular and sufficiently large, then, by the breakthrough work of Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown, they admit a decomposition into Hamilton cycles and at most one perfect matching, solving the well-known Nash-Williams conjecture. In the pseudorandom setting, it has long been conjectured that similar results hold in much sparser graphs. We prove two overarching theorems for graphs that exclude excessively dense subgraphs, which yield asymptotically optimal resilience and Hamilton-decomposition results in sparse pseudorandom graphs. First, our results imply that for every fixed $γ>0$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that if $G$ is a spanning subgraph of an $(n,d,λ)$-graph satisfying $δ(G)\ge\bigl(\tfrac12+γ\bigr)d$ and $ d/λ\ge C,$ then $G$ must contain a Hamilton cycle. Second, we show that for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $C>0$ so that any $(n,d,λ)$-graph $G$ with $d/λ\ge C$ contains at least $\bigl(1-\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, and, finally, we prove that the entire edge set of $G$ can be covered by no more than $\bigl(1+\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ such cycles. All bounds are asymptotically optimal and significantly improve earlier results on Hamiltonian resilience, packing, and covering in sparse pseudorandom graphs.

papers.name: Optimal control of SDEs with merely measurable drift: an HJB approach
papers.abstract: We investigate an optimal control problem for a diffusion whose drift and running cost are merely measurable in the state variable. Such low regularity rules out the use of Pontryagin's maximum principle and also invalidates the standard proof of the Bellman principle of optimality. We address these difficulties by analyzing the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Working in a weak formulation of admissible controls, we first establish the state-equation solvability and Krylov estimates needed to make the control problem well defined. Using PDE techniques together with a policy iteration scheme, we prove that the HJB equation admits a unique strong solution, and this solution coincides with the value function of the control problem. Based on this identification, we establish a verification theorem and recover the Bellman optimality principle without imposing any additional smoothness assumptions. We further investigate a mollification scheme depending on a parameter $\varepsilon > 0$. It turns out that the smoothed value functions $V_{\varepsilon}$ may fail to converge to the original value function $V$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, and we provide an explicit counterexample. To resolve this, we identify a structural condition on the control set. When the control set is countable, convergence $V_{\varepsilon} \to V$ holds locally uniformly.

papers.name: A Higgs category for the cluster variety of triples of flags
papers.abstract: The cluster variety of triples of flags (associated with a split simple Lie group of Dynkin type Delta) plays a key role in higher Teichmuller theory as developed by Fock-Goncharov, Jiarui Fei, Ian Le, ... and Goncharov-Shen. We refer to it as the basic triangle associated with Delta. In this paper, for simply laced Delta, we construct and study a Higgs category (in the sense of Yilin Wu) which we expect to categorify the basic triangle. This category is a certain exact dg category (in the sense of Xiaofa Chen) which is Frobenius and stably 2-Calabi-Yau. We show that it has indeed the expected cyclic group symmetry and that its derived category has the expected braid group symmetry. A key ingredient in our construction is a conjecture by Merlin Christ, whose proof occupies most of this paper. The proof is based on a new description of the Higgs category in terms of Gorenstein projective dg modules. Our techniques are in the spirit of Orlov in his work on triangulated categories of graded B-branes.

papers.name: Optimal Algorithms for Nonlinear Estimation with Convex Models
papers.abstract: A linear functional of an object from a convex symmetric set can be optimally estimated, in a worst-case sense, by a linear functional of observations made on the object. This well-known fact is extended here to a nonlinear setting: other simple functionals of the object can be optimally estimated by functionals of the observations that share a similar simple structure. This is established for the maximum of several linear functionals and even for the $\ell$th largest among them. Proving the latter requires an unusual variation of the analytical Hahn--Banach theorem. The existence results are accompanied by practical recipes relying on convex optimization to construct the desired functionals, thereby justifying the term of estimation algorithms.

papers.name: State integrals for the quantized $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Chern-Simons invariant
papers.abstract: Previous work of the author and N.\ Reshetikhin defines an invariant $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^ψ(K, ρ, μ)$ of a knot $K$, a representation $ρ\colon π_{1}(S^{3} \setminus K) \to \operatorname{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$, and a logarithm $μ$ of a meridian eigenvalue of $ρ$. It can be interpreted as a geometric twist of the Kashaev invariant or as a quantization of the $\operatorname{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{C})$ Chern-Simons invariant and is defined via a discrete state-sum involving quantum dilogarithms. In this paper we show how to express $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^ψ(K, ρ, μ)$ as a sum over contour integrals in a space parametrizing hyperbolic structures on the knot complement. Such state integral presentations are an important step in determining the asymptotics of quantum invariants as predicted by the Volume Conjecture. We discuss this perspective and the remaining obstacles to establishing exponential growth of $\operatorname{Z}_{N}^ψ$.

papers.name: Gödel-Tarski Translation for Constructive Logics with Transitive Closure
papers.abstract: We introduce the semantically-defined constructive propositional dynamic logics of regular programs $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$, respectively extending the basic constructive modal logic $\sf CK$ and its Wijesekera-style variant $\sf WK$. Using translations between our logics and $\sf PDL$, we show that both $\sf CPDL$ and $\sf WPDL$ are {\sc ExpTime}-complete and enjoy an exponential-size finite model property. In particular, their diamond-free fragment, restricted to a single atomic program and its reflexive transitive closure is already {\sc ExpTime}-complete, thereby settling the conjecture of Afshari et al. By embedding $\sf CS4$ and $\sf WS4$ into our logics, we show their validity problems are also in {\sc ExpTime}, improving the previously known {\sc NExpTime} upper bound obtained via finite model arguments.

papers.name: A Direct Approach to Rough Differential Equations Driven by Controlled Rough Paths
papers.abstract: We study rough differential equations driven by controlled rough paths. Given a rough path $\mathbf X$ and an $\mathbf X$-controlled rough path $\mathbf Z$, we develop a direct controlled rough paths approach to the rough differential equation $dY_t=F(Y_t)\,d\mathbf Z_t$. More specifically, we establish rough integral estimates and the universal limit theorem directly in the space of $\X$-controlled rough paths.

papers.name: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.

papers.name: Infinitely many associated primes of local cohomology modules of ramified regular local rings
papers.abstract: We construct examples of local cohomology modules of ramified regular local rings with infinitely many associated primes and infinite Bass numbers.

papers.name: A Mathematical Characterization of Neural Activation Induced by Temporal Interference Stimulation
papers.abstract: Temporal Interference Stimulation (TIS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique in which two high-frequency sinusoidal currents with slightly different frequencies generate a low-frequency envelope that can activate deep neural structures. This study investigates the conditions under which TIS elicits action potentials in a single neuron modeled by the FitzHugh-Nagumo system. This research integrates phase-plane analysis and geometric singular perturbation to develop a mathematical framework for analyzing TIS. By combining a mathematical analysis of differential equations with computer simulations, the study elucidates how the amplitudes and beat frequency jointly determine whether the neuron remains quiescent, exhibits only transient responses, or undergoes persistent (tonic) firing.

papers.name: Accelerating Sinkhorn for Entropy-Regularized Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Entropy-regularized optimal transport is widely used to compare and align data distributions, but Sinkhorn can converge slowly at small regularization. We introduce Acc-Sinkhorn, a two-state Hessian-driven Nesterov iteration built on the dual mirror geometry of the row-reduced Sinkhorn map. The method combines momentum acceleration with an inexpensive descent safeguard, stable log-domain evaluation, and a prescribed homotopy schedule requiring neither line search nor curvature estimation. We prove global linear convergence of the safeguarded method, rule out consecutive restarts, and establish local accelerated convergence for fixed parameters without restarts through spectral analysis. Numerical comparisons with six methods on synthetic problems, color transfer, and bilingual word alignment show runtime speedups of up to about 26 over Sinkhorn, with additional rendering-accuracy comparisons for color transfer.

papers.name: Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
papers.abstract: The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data. Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.

papers.name: A closed subspace of a Gateaux differentiability space is a Gateaux differentiability space : over 46 years of open problem solved
papers.abstract: This paper establishes, for the first time, an iterative and rigid theory of weak\(^{*}\) slices in a non-metric setting, demonstrating that dual convex sets admit localization, diameter control and fine structural analysis under the pure weak\(^{*}\) topology. It fundamentally reshapes the classical perspective on the geometric features of the weak\(^{*}\) topology and thereby pioneers a new direction in non-metric weak\(^{*}\) slice geometry. Using a novel technique built upon intricate manipulation of weak\(^{*}\) slices and a carefully engineered iterative selection scheme, we prove that if $M$ is a closed subspace of a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space $X$, then $M$ itself is a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space. As a corollary, we obtain that if $X$ is a weak Asplund space and $M$ is a closed subspace of $X$, then $M$ is a G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability space. This settles definitively an open problem posed 46 years ago by D.G. Larman and R.R. Phelps (J. London Math. Soc., 20 (1979), 115-127).

papers.name: Pathwise Uniqueness for Cyclically Catalytic Branching Diffusions
papers.abstract: We study pathwise uniqueness for cyclic catalytic stochastic differential equations whose state-dependent square-root diffusion coefficients are non-Lipschitz and degenerate on the boundary. The approach is the direct construction of a strong solution using a Malliavin compactness criterion. The key is the development of a new family of boundary-sensitive weighted Malliavin estimates for the tangent processes of the smooth approximations. Pathwise uniqueness then follows from the dual Yamada-Watanabe argument together with the weak uniqueness available in the literature.

papers.name: An Orlicz variational formula for David-type Beltrami equations
papers.abstract: We develop a Banach-space variational theory for degenerate Beltrami equations of David type. For coefficients supported in a bounded domain $\mathcal{U}\subset\mathbb{C}$, the pointwise change of variables $ν=2μ/(1-|μ|^2)$ identifies the David coefficients with the exponential Orlicz space $L^Φ_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ for $Φ(s)=e^s-s-1$. On the open subset of parameters with a sufficiently large exponential moment, the principal solution map is locally real $C^{1,1}$ into $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{C})$, with Fréchet derivative solving the linearized Beltrami equation. On the Orlicz heart $E^Φ_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ it is real $C^\infty$, yet fails to be real analytic at zero: along any direction $h$, its Taylor series at zero has radius of convergence $1/\|h\|_\infty$ in $W^{1,2}(B)$ for every disk $B\supset\overline{\mathcal{U}}$. Finally, for $\mathcal{U}=\mathbb{D}$, the exterior Schwarzian map from $E^Φ_{\mathbb{D}}(\mathbb{C})$ to the little logarithmic Bers space is continuous, but fails to be Fréchet differentiable at zero; moreover, its zero fiber is not a $C^1$ embedded Banach submanifold near zero, obstructing any local $C^1$ split submersion structure on the resulting quotient.

papers.name: A note on 4-forms in 8-dimensions
papers.abstract: We present a note on two related questions on 4-forms in 8-dimensions. In particular, we give explicit families of 4-forms, beyond the Cayley and quaternion-Kähler forms, which determine a metric via the formula of Karigiannis. Additionally, we discuss an open question of Salamon and Walpuski on non-degenerate 4-forms, and answer it for a more restrictive notion of non-degeneracy.

papers.name: Counterexamples to Peskine-Szpiro's conjectures on modules of finite projective dimension
papers.abstract: We give counterexamples to the remaining homological conjectures of Peskine-Szpiro concerning modules of finite projective dimension over Noetherian local rings. Specifically, we show that the dimension inequality, the strong intersection conjecture, and the grade conjecture are all false in general.

papers.name: On the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm in spaces generated by Rademacher functions and their $p$-adic analogues
papers.abstract: Sufficient conditions for the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm in the space spanned by generalized Rademacher functions are proved. It is shown that the sufficient number of nodes for discretization with the minimal number of nodes is equal to $N$ or $N+1$ and depends on the dimension $N$. The conjecture of F.~Dai, A.~Prymak, V.~N.~Temlyakov, and S.~Yu.~Tikhonov on the positivity of weights in the exact discretization of the $L_2$-norm with a minimal number of points considered. It was investigated in which cases it holds and in which it fails for the spaces spanned by the $N$ generalized Rademacher functions with base $p$, and how the validity of the conjecture in this case depends on the parameters $p$ and $N$. The connection with generalized Hadamard matrices, the Hadamard's conjecture and Seberry's conjecture is demonstrated.

papers.name: Maximal first Betti number drop and collapsing RCD spaces
papers.abstract: Let $(X_i,d_i,\mathfrak m_i)$ be compact $\mathrm{RCD}(K,N)$ spaces converging to a space $X$ of rectifiable dimension $m$. Their first Betti numbers can drop by at most $N-m$. When equality holds, the maximal abelian covers have a non-collapsed limit $Y$ carrying a free isometric $\mathbb{R}^{N-m}$-action. We turn this limiting symmetry into fibrations of the approximating spaces. More precisely, after passing to a subsequence, there is an open full-measure set $G\subset X$, containing every regular point, on which $X$ is a topological orbifold and the $X_i$ admit local Seifert fibrations with $(N-m)$-torus fibres. Each finite local group acts on the fibre by translations. If the $X_i$ have no boundary, then $X\setminus G$ has Hausdorff codimension at least two. If $Y$ has no bubbling and $X$ is a smooth closed Riemannian orbifold, the local fibrations may be chosen as restrictions of a single global Seifert fibration. A global orbit coordinate on the smooth manifold cover shows, in addition, that this fibration is the orbit map of a continuous torus action and becomes a product with $\mathbb{T}^{N-m}$ on finite covers of $X_i$ and $X$ of a fixed degree, as Peng, Wang and Wang proved for smooth torus bundles at the Betti number equality. When the base is a closed Riemannian manifold, the maps are principal torus bundles; this confirms a conjecture of Zamora and Zhu for possibly singular $\mathrm{RCD}$ total spaces. The new ingredients are a pointwise linearization of the collapsing action at regular orbits, an invariant harmonic transverse coordinate compatible with finite isotropy, and an exactly equivariant orbit coordinate built from an elementary rounding-and-doubling argument in the collapsing deck group.

papers.name: An adaptive $L_2$-type test for high-dimensional white noise
papers.abstract: We propose a new $L_2$-type test for white noise which allows the dimension $p$ of the time series to either (i) be a fixed constant, or (ii) diverge with the sample size $n$. The proposed test statistic exhibits an interesting phase transition, following two different regimes of behavior: $p$ is fixed, and $p\rightarrow\infty$. Because identification of the operable regime is difficult, if not impossible in practice, we devise a novel adaptive bootstrap method to construct a unified testing procedure across different phases. Numerical experiments confirm the good finite sample performance of the proposed adaptive $L_2$-type test in comparison to the existing methods in the literature. The proposed testing procedure has been implemented in R package HDTSA.

papers.name: Non-Hermitian Yang--Mills Connections with Vanishing Chern Classes
papers.abstract: We construct non-flat non-Hermitian Yang--Mills connections with vanishing Chern classes whose induced and conjugate-dual holomorphic bundles are both stable, giving a negative answer to Kaledin and Verbitsky's flatness question even under these stability assumptions. We also give negative answers to their questions about the étaleness and bijectivity of the harmonic-class map. The examples are explicit connections on smoothly trivial rank-two bundles over projective Kähler surfaces and admit explicit positive harmonic metrics. For the family of fixed stable bundles studied here, the harmonic-class map is surjective. Every fibre contains exactly one flat point, but some fibres also contain positive-dimensional families of non-flat connections. The entire flat locus is a smooth component mapped biholomorphically onto the target. For a range of parameters, we determine the complete reduced analytic germ at a distinguished nonunitary flat point. It has two smooth branches of different dimensions whose intersection contains two-sided stable points arbitrarily close to that point. Finally, a single fibre of the pair of holomorphic projections contains infinitely many flat classes and an embedded copy of $\CC^*$ with exactly two flat members. Thus the two holomorphic isomorphism classes together do not determine flatness.

papers.name: Transcending Algebraic Geometry
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of some of the ideas leading up to Jacob Tsimerman's groundbreaking work developing the theory of o-minimal definability in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

papers.name: Plunge bounds for Fourier concentration operators: geometry, smoothing, and wave packets
papers.abstract: We prove a single-logarithm bound for the eigenvalues in the plunge region of Fourier concentration operators, removing the extra logarithmic factor in the Kulikov--Dam Larsen bound for two general admissible sets throughout each fixed exponential window. For bounded spatial and frequency sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of positive measure with finite upper codimension-one Minkowski boundary content, the number $Λ_\varepsilon(cA,B)$ of eigenvalues in $(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)$ satisfies $Λ_\varepsilon(cA,B)\le C(d,A,B,β)c^{d-1}D(1+\log_+(c/D))$, where $D=\log(1/(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)))$, for every fixed $β>0$, $c\ge2$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and $D\leβc$, with $\log_+t=\max(0,\log t)$. The argument uses positive band-limited smoothing and requires no symmetry, convexity, or connectedness. In dimension two, the corresponding exponential-window estimate has a constant uniform in the window parameter. We also determine the optimal coordinate-Lipschitz constant $d-1$ for recursive decompositions of balls and standard simplices in every dimension, and obtain box-frequency estimates with explicit geometric constants. For $C^1$ convex bodies in three dimensions, the optimal infimum of recursive coordinate slopes is $2$. Uniform real-order Bessel estimates give independent disk and ball bounds at every spectral threshold, including an explicit deep-tail term. For smooth strictly convex planar frequency bodies with positive curvature, we prove correlation estimates for aligned Gaussian packets at arbitrary relative scales and quantitative lower bounds on the cost of estimating spatial blocks separately. Together these results connect the global spectral bound with sharp geometric constructions and the cancellation retained by grouping boundary interactions.

papers.name: S-squareful values of binary quadratic forms
papers.abstract: Shute showed that the leading constant in the asymptotic formula for squareful values of the form $ax^2+by^2$ does not match with the conjecture established by Pieropan, Smeets, Tanimoto and Várilly-Alvarado. In this paper, $S$-squareful values of this form are considered for $S$ the set of primes that divide $a$ and $b$. We prove an asymptotic formula for these numbers and show that the leading constant of the asymptotic formula still does not match the conjecture. Furthermore, we consider the updated conjecture established by Chow, Loughran, Takloo-Bighash, and Tanimoto regarding the leading constant for Campana points in the given setting and show that this constant is consistent with our computed constant.

papers.name: Optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems
papers.abstract: We design and test optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems. Each method is A-stable, implicit, and second-order accurate. We focus on achieving the smallest possible error constant while also ensuring that stiff modes are damped. We recover some known optimal L-stable three- and four-step methods and prove their global optimality, and provide a new five-step method with essentially optimal error constant. We also study methods that are not L-stable but provide a prescribed rate of damping in the infinitely stiff limit; in particular, we prove that a known two-step family is optimal. Variable-step-size formulae are also provided for the L-stable methods. Numerical tests demonstrate that the improved error constants lead to improved accuracy.

papers.name: On the Hodge conjecture for hyper-Kähler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by four
papers.abstract: We prove the Hodge conjecture for all hyper-Kähler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by 4 and all of their powers. To this end, we show that such hyper-Kähler varieties are homologically motivated by their intermediate Jacobians.

papers.name: On the median of the beta distribution in relation to the median of the gamma distribution
papers.abstract: The median of the beta distribution has no closed form, but it is closely tied to the median of the gamma distribution. Kerman's approximation has the ratio form $g(α)/(g(α)+g(β))$ with $g(x) = x - 1/3$, a lower bound on the gamma median, and it is a lower bound on the beta median for $1/3 < α< β$. The ratio form built from the true gamma median is a tighter lower bound, asymptotically exact as $β\to \infty$. The ratio form built from the Wilson-Hilferty approximation to the gamma median, implicit in a classical approximation to the $F$ distribution but little known as an approximation to the beta median, is an upper bound on the line $α= 1$ and, along each ray $β= rα$ with $r > 1$, for large shape parameters. The ratio form that is exact on the lines $α= 1$ and $β= 1$, $(2^{1/β} - 1)/(2^{1/α} + 2^{1/β} - 2)$, is numerically within 0.3% of the median when both shape parameters are at least 1, and provably less than 25% above it for $α\le β$; it yields a new approximation to the gamma median, which is an upper bound on it for shape parameter below 1 and a lower bound above 1. Interpolating between it and a ratio form with a $1/x$ correction gives, with no fitted constant, an approximation within 0.016% of the median when both shape parameters are at least 1. No ratio form gives the beta median exactly. For large shape parameters, the logit of the median has an explicit second-order expansion. For small shape parameters, bounds in elementary functions are asymptotically tight. An approximation in elementary functions that joins the two ends, with four fitted constants, is exact on the lines $α= 1$, $β= 1$, and $α= β$, and numerically within 0.065% of the median over the whole domain. Most of the proofs are machine-verified in Lean 4.

papers.name: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
papers.abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.

papers.name: Generalized Wishart processes under nonlinear expectation
papers.abstract: We develop a theory of generalized Wishart processes within the framework of $G$-expectation, with $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and the $G$-Wishart process as two typical examples. In contrast to the classical setting, we show that $G$-Dyson Brownian motion may exhibit collisions and provide a sufficient condition ensuring the non-collision property of the eigenvalues of generalized Wishart processes. We then derive the equations governing the high-dimensional limits of the empirical spectral measures under $G$-expectation, leading to the corresponding semicircle law for $G$-Dyson Brownian motion and Marchenko--Pastur law for the $G$-Wishart process.

papers.name: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
papers.abstract: We study strong positivity and Hodge--Riemann relations for real $(1,1)$-forms satisfying generalized $m$-positivity conditions. Every good prefix, defined via the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant, has a strictly strongly positive product and satisfies the Hodge--Riemann relations in all bidegrees. Allowing boundary factors, we prove that the hyperbolicity cone of every nonzero product of an almost-good prefix coincides with the polarizing component of its exterior-algebra quotient. As a special case, we obtain the full mixed Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary $m$-positive forms without assuming semipositivity. We also establish the Hodge--Riemann relations for weakly $(m,l)$-positive forms in all bidegrees $(p,q)$ with $p+q\le m$ and $\max\{p,q\}\ge l$. For $l=1$ and $m\ge2$, we deduce that the associated $(m-1)$-th power map is a real-analytic diffeomorphism onto the cone of strictly positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Adapting the $L^2$ method of Dinh and Nguyên, we pass from these pointwise results to the cohomology of compact Kähler manifolds. Finally, we study numerical criteria, generalized complex Hessian equations, and sharp reverse Khovanskii--Teissier inequalities in the sequential setting.

papers.name: Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
papers.abstract: We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.

papers.name: Uniform symmetric spectral finiteness of cones definable in o-minimal structures
papers.abstract: Cone-constrained eigenvalues of a matrix are defined by a complementarity problem over a closed convex cone. We show that every closed convex cone that is definable in an o-minimal structure is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite; that is, the cone spectra of symmetric matrices relative to the cone (the sets of their cone-constrained eigenvalues) have uniformly bounded cardinality. In particular, we derive explicit uniform bounds for semialgebraic cones, and the explicit uniform bound we obtain for a Löwner cone depends only on the order of the matrices in the cone. Using the uniform finiteness of cone spectra, we also show that the number of singular values relative to two closed convex cones definable in a common o-minimal structure is uniformly bounded. Finally, we provide a closed convex cone that is not definable in any o-minimal structure and for which the spectra of symmetric matrices are finite but have no uniform cardinality bound.

papers.name: Minimal Control Time of Large Generic Quantum Systems at Critical Spectral Growth
papers.abstract: The minimal time needed to steer a closed quantum system between two arbitrary states is a fundamental performance limit of quantum control. For single-input bilinear Schrödinger systems of dimension $d$ with unbounded controls, this state-to-state control time is bounded from above by the weight $M_d$ of a minimum spanning tree (MST) built from the drift Hamiltonian written in the eigenbasis of the control Hamiltonian.
